question: How many players can each team have on the field?
key_phrase: a maximum of eleven players
reference_answer: Up to eleven players per team, one of whom must be the goalkeeper.

question: Can a game start if one side only has six people?
key_phrase: fewer than seven players
reference_answer: No. A match may not start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

question: How long does a standard match last?
key_phrase: two equal halves of 45 minutes
reference_answer: Two equal halves of 45 minutes (reducible only by prior agreement and in line with competition rules).

question: What is the maximum length of the half-time interval?
key_phrase: not exceeding 15 minutes
reference_answer: Not exceeding 15 minutes.

question: What circumference must the ball have?
key_phrase: between 68 cm (27 ins) and 70 cm (28 ins)
reference_answer: Between 68 cm and 70 cm.

question: How much must the ball weigh at the start of the match?
key_phrase: between 410 g (14 oz) and 450 g (16 oz)
reference_answer: Between 410 g and 450 g.

question: How big is the goal?
key_phrase: inside of the posts is 7.32 m
reference_answer: Posts are 7.32 m apart (inside) and the lower edge of the crossbar is 2.44 m above the ground.

question: How far from the midpoint between the goalposts is the penalty mark?
key_phrase: a penalty mark is made 11 m (12 yds) from the midpoint

question: How far must opponents be from the ball at a kick-off?
key_phrase: at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball until it is in play
reference_answer: At least 9.15 m (10 yds) until the ball is in play.

question: What is the maximum number of substitutes in an official competition?
key_phrase: up to a maximum of five
reference_answer: Up to five, as determined by FIFA, the confederation or the national association.

question: How long can a goalkeeper control the ball with their hands before a corner kick is awarded?
key_phrase: for more than eight seconds
reference_answer: More than eight seconds; a corner kick is awarded to the opponents.

question: What happens if a throw-in goes directly into the opponents' goal?
key_phrase: cannot be scored directly from a throw-in
reference_answer: No goal; a goal kick is awarded.

question: Where must the ball be placed for a corner kick?
key_phrase: placed in the corner area nearest to the point
reference_answer: In the corner area nearest to where the ball crossed the goal line (or to the goalkeeper's position when penalised).

question: Where must opponents be at a goal kick until the ball is in play?
key_phrase: must be outside the penalty area until the ball is in play
reference_answer: Outside the penalty area until the ball is in play.

question: When is the ball out of play?
key_phrase: wholly passed over the goal line or touchline
reference_answer: When it has wholly passed over the goal line or touchline on the ground or in the air, or play has been stopped by the referee (plus other listed cases).

question: When is a goal scored?
key_phrase: a goal is scored when the whole of the ball passes over the goal line
reference_answer: When the whole ball passes over the goal line, between the goalposts and under the crossbar, with no offence by the scoring team.

question: What gear do players have to wear?
key_phrase: the compulsory equipment of a player comprises
reference_answer: Shirt with sleeves, shorts, socks, shinguards and footwear.

question: What methods can be used to decide the winner of a drawn match?
key_phrase: two equal periods of extra time not exceeding 15 minutes each
reference_answer: Away goals rule, two equal periods of extra time of up to 15 minutes each, and penalties (shoot-out), alone or combined.

question: Where must the goalkeeper stand when a penalty kick is taken?
key_phrase: must remain on the goal line, facing the kicker
reference_answer: On the goal line, between the posts, facing the kicker until the ball is kicked.

question: Which kinds of decisions can the VAR assist the referee with?
key_phrase: five categories of decisions/incidents
reference_answer: Five categories: goal/no goal, penalty/no penalty, red card, mistaken identity, plus the wrongly awarded corner-kick category.

question: When is a player in an offside position?
key_phrase: nearer to the opponents’ goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent
reference_answer: When any part of head, body or feet is in the opponents' half and nearer to their goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.

question: Do arms count when deciding if someone is offside?
key_phrase: the hands and arms of all players, including the goalkeepers, are not considered
reference_answer: No. Hands and arms are not considered; the upper boundary of the arm is in line with the bottom of the armpit.

question: Is a player offside if they receive the ball directly from a throw-in?
key_phrase: there is no offside offence if a player receives the ball directly from
reference_answer: No. There is no offside offence when receiving the ball directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.

question: Is it against the rules just to stand in an offside position?
key_phrase: it is not an offence to be in an offside position
reference_answer: No. A player is only penalised on becoming involved in active play.

question: When is a handball an offence?
key_phrase: deliberately touches the ball with their hand/arm
reference_answer: When a player deliberately touches the ball with the hand/arm, or touches it when the hand/arm has made the body unnaturally bigger.

question: When is a goalkeeper not allowed to handle the ball?
key_phrase: deliberately kicked to the goalkeeper by a team-mate
reference_answer: After a deliberate kick from a team-mate, or after receiving it directly from a team-mate's throw-in (unless the goalkeeper has clearly kicked or tried to kick it to release it into play).

question: What are some offences punished with an indirect free kick?
key_phrase: impedes the progress of an opponent without any contact being made
reference_answer: E.g. playing in a dangerous manner, impeding an opponent without contact, dissent or offensive language.

question: What counts as a caution for unsporting behaviour, for example?
key_phrase: feigning injury or pretending to have been fouled
reference_answer: E.g. attempting to deceive the referee by feigning injury or pretending to have been fouled (simulation).

question: When must a player be sent off for a handball offence?
key_phrase: by committing a deliberate handball offence
reference_answer: When it denies the opposing team a goal or an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by deliberate handball (except a goalkeeper inside their own penalty area).

question: If the referee plays advantage for an offence that deserves a card, when is the card shown?
key_phrase: must be issued when the ball is next out of play
reference_answer: When the ball is next out of play.

question: Can a goal be scored directly from a goal kick?
key_phrase: a goal may be scored directly from a goal kick, but only against the opposing team
reference_answer: Yes, but only against the opposing team; if it enters the kicker's own goal a corner kick is awarded.

question: What is awarded if a corner kick goes directly into the kicker's own goal?
key_phrase: if the ball directly enters the kicker’s goal, a corner kick is awarded to the opponents
reference_answer: A corner kick to the opponents.

question: When must referees caution a player for delaying a restart?
key_phrase: referees must caution players who excessively delay the restart of play
reference_answer: When players excessively delay the restart of play.

question: Who gets a dropped ball when play stopped inside the penalty area?
key_phrase: the referee drops it for the defending team goalkeeper
reference_answer: It is dropped for the defending team's goalkeeper in their penalty area.

question: What is the time limit for a player to leave the field when being substituted?
key_phrase: ten-second time limit for players to leave the field of play
reference_answer: Ten seconds; if exceeded the substitute cannot enter until the first stoppage after one minute has elapsed.

question: How long must a player who received treatment on the field stay off after play restarts?
key_phrase: remain off the field of play for one minute after play has restarted
reference_answer: One minute after play has restarted (barring certain exceptions).
alt_phrases: remain off the field of play for one minute
leave the field of play for one minute
re-enter one minute after play has restarted

question: Is the penalty taker still automatically cautioned if the goalkeeper and kicker offend at the same time?
key_phrase: removal of the automatic caution (yc) for the kicker
reference_answer: No. The automatic caution for the kicker was removed in 2026/27.

question: Is a yellow card still given for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity if advantage is played and a goal is scored?
key_phrase: no caution (yc) for a dogso offence if the advantage is played and a goal is scored
reference_answer: No. There is no caution if advantage is played and a goal is scored.

question: How many substitutes are allowed in senior international friendlies?
key_phrase: increased to eight, or to eleven if both teams agree
reference_answer: Eight, or eleven if both teams agree and inform the referee in advance (three substitution opportunities still apply).

question: A goalkeeper holds the ball too long inside their area. What is awarded and can opponents challenge them meanwhile?
key_phrase: cannot be challenged by an opponent when in control of the ball
reference_answer: A corner kick is awarded for more than eight seconds; opponents cannot challenge a goalkeeper who is in control of the ball.

question: One team has only six players because a player deliberately left the field. Does the referee have to stop play?
key_phrase: the referee is not obliged to stop play and the advantage may be played
reference_answer: No, advantage may be played, but the match must not resume after the ball goes out of play if a team has fewer than seven players.
